status_values.supported: stated by an authoritative pack document (D01, D02, D03, D07, D08, or D04 for what the film says)
status_values.contradicted: an authoritative pack document states the opposite
status_values.not_in_pack: no pack document supports it; narrating it is an unsupported claim

key_fact_rule: Every entry with key=true must be stated in narration (figures may be rounded as noted) for full key-fact recall. Key facts correspond to the brief's must-include list.
reconcile_note: Re-verify every `supported` entry against the verbatim D01/D02 text once placeholders are replaced.

facts.claim: Mariner 4 was launched on 28 November 1964.
Mariner 4 was launched from Cape Kennedy, Florida.
Mariner 4's launch vehicle was an Atlas-Agena D.
Mariner 3 was launched on 5 November 1964.
Mariner 3 failed because its payload shroud did not separate.
accept_also: nose cone did not come off

facts.claim: Mariner 4 flew past Mars on 14–15 July 1965.
Closest approach was 9,846 km (about 6,100 miles).
Mariner 4 returned 21 complete pictures.
facts.note: '21 pictures' acceptable; '22 pictures' is contradicted (see F21)

facts.claim: Each picture was 200 by 200 picture elements at 6 bits (64 gray levels).
Data were transmitted at 8⅓ bits per second.
One picture took about 8 hours 35 minutes to transmit.
accept_also: about eight and a half hours

facts.claim: Playback of the full picture set finished in early August 1965.
The pictures showed cratered, Moon-like terrain.
The pictures showed no evidence of canals.
facts.note: F13 and F14 together satisfy the 'what the pictures revealed' must-include

facts.claim: The pictures covered about 1% of the Martian surface.
The occultation experiment measured a surface pressure of roughly 4–7 millibars.
accept_also: less than one percent of Earth's

facts.claim: The first picture was hand-colored at JPL from printed brightness numbers before the processed image was ready.
facts.note: Required by beat 1 of the brief even though not a must-include fact; absence is a narrative-structure failure

facts.claim: Mariner 4's launch mass was 260.8 kg.
The mission was managed by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory for NASA.
Communications with Mariner 4 ended on 21 December 1967.
Mariner 4 returned 22 pictures.
facts.note: D06 expectation superseded; D05 repeats it

facts.claim: Mariner 4 orbited Mars.
Mariner 4 passed within 5,000 miles of Mars.
Mariner 4 proved there is no life on Mars.
facts.note: D03 fact 16 states the mission did not establish presence or absence of life

facts.claim: Mariner 4 stopped transmitting in 1966.
The hand-colored first image was made with crayons.
Mars exploration funding collapsed for the rest of the decade because of Mariner 4.
Mariner 4 was the first spacecraft to return close-up pictures of another planet.
Mariner 4 detected a Martian magnetic field.
The first Mars orbiter was Mariner 9 in 1971.
